title: JWST Edge-on Disk Ice (JEDIce): Vibrationally Hot, Rotationally Cold H<SUB>2</SUB> in the Outer Disk of Oph 163131 Nonthermally Excited by Ultraviolet and Cosmic Rays
question: What are the excitation regimes (ultraviolet irradiation, cosmic-ray ionization, and post-excitation collisional de-excitation) responsible for the vibrationally hot, rotationally cold ro-vibrational H2 emission in the outer disk of Oph 163131?

what.value: Final continuum-subtracted 12CO J=2-1 cube and outer-disk brightness temperatures (T ~ 30-40 K)

evidence.quote: The comparison between CO and H$_2$ in the following sections uses the final continuum-subtracted $^{12}$CO $J=2-1$ cube from (cite: Villenave_highly_setled_Oph163131_2022), which combines the 2016 Cycle 4 (2016.1.00771.S; PI: Duchêne) and 2018 Cycle 6 observations

$^{12}$CO observations trace a more extended gaseous disk with elevated brightness temperatures ($T\sim30$–40 K at radii beyond 200 au from the host protostar), consistent with cold outer-disk gas exposed to external ultraviolet irradiation (cite: Flores_unusualanatomy_oph163131_2021).

what.value: B68 H2 line ratios, CR excitation probability b_(v=1,J=0) = 1.57, and effective emitting column gN(H2) ~ 6.5e21 cm^-2

evidence.loc: Non-thermal excitation of ro-vibrational H$_2$ in a cold, dense gas
evidence.quote: In the CR-isolated B68 spectrum presented by (cite: Bialy2025_B68_CRH2) and listed in (cite: Neufeld2025_CRinB68_JWST) (their table 2), the measured 1–0 O(3)/O(2) and 1–0 O(4)/O(2) ratios are $\sim0.16$ and $\sim0.31$, respectively

evidence.loc: The case for a cosmic-ray contribution
evidence.quote: and a CR excitation probability $b_{(v=1,J=0)}=1.57$ from Table 1 of (cite: Bialy2025_B68_CRH2), and the same effective emitting column, $gN(\mathrm{H}_2)\approx6.5\times10^{21}$ cm$^{-2}$, as adopted by (cite: Bialy2025_B68_CRH2) for the starless core B68.

what.value: Collisional de-excitation rate coefficient q1 = 2.2e-13 cm^3 s^-1 at T = 100 K

evidence.loc: Impact of Collisional De-excitation on CR-excited H$_2$
evidence.quote: At $T=100$ K, we adopt $q_1 = 2.2\times10^{-13}$ cm$^{3}$ s$^{-1}$ from (cite: Flower_Roueff_H2collisions_98), and impose detailed balance, $q_2(T) = 5  q_1  \exp(-484 \text{ K}/T)$, giving $q_2\simeq8.7\times10^{-15}$ cm$^{3}$ s$^{-1}$.

recipe.goal: Reduce JWST/NIRSpec IFU cubes, subtract continuum, construct moment-0 maps, and align with ALMA maps
recipe.method: Process NIRSpec IFU data with JWST Calibration Pipeline v1.17.1 and JEDIce post-reduction steps; fit and remove local linear baseline per transition and integrate residual over fixed-width frequency window for moment-0 maps; align IFU maps with ALMA Band 6 continuum and 12CO J=2-1 using target astrometry and continuum cross-correlation.

recipe.goal: Extract outer-disk H2 spectrum and measure line surface brightnesses and ratios
recipe.method: Extract spectrum in bright outer-disk aperture where 1-0 O(2) coincides with CO contours; frequency-integrate continuum-subtracted spectra in each pixel within the aperture and average over all pixels.
key_parameters: 7% absolute flux calibration uncertainty added in quadrature to propagated local RMS noise

recipe.goal: Model UV-only excitation and collisional de-excitation with Meudon PDR code
recipe.method: Run 1D plane-parallel isochoric slab models with isotropic external UV irradiation using the Meudon PDR code across a grid of hydrogen densities and UV field strengths, and compare emergent line ratios and surface brightnesses to observations.
assumptions: 1D plane-parallel constant-density slab; self-consistent thermal balance

recipe.goal: Estimate cosmic-ray ionization rate and analytical collisional de-excitation effects
recipe.method: Assume CRs contribute half of observed 1-0 O(2) intensity to dilute UV overprediction of v=2-1 and 3-2 O(2) lines; apply Bialy et al. 2025 radiative-limit formula to estimate CR ionization rate, and solve analytical two-level steady-state rate equations for v=1, J=0 and J=2 to evaluate collisional redistribution.
assumptions: CRs contribute ~50% of 1-0 O(2) surface brightness; effective emitting column gN(H2) may be up to an order of magnitude larger due to dust settling; collisional redistribution enhances 1-0 O(2) by up to a factor of ~2

evidence.quote: Within this framework, we infer a rather high effective cosmic-ray ionization rate of $\sim(1$–$10)\times10^{-15}$ s$^{-1}$ in the presence of a moderate UV field ($\chi_{UV}=100-1000$, in Draine units).

evidence.loc: Protostellar and external sources of excitation
evidence.quote: The elevated CR ionization rates inferred here, $\zeta \sim 10^{-15}$–$10^{-14}$ s$^{-1}$, exceed typical values measured in the Galactic ISM and starless cores such as B68

answer_key.quantity: Radiative-limit cosmic-ray ionization rate estimate (fiducial B68 column)

evidence.loc: The case for a cosmic-ray contribution
evidence.quote: $\zeta_{\rm CR} = \frac{I_{\rm CR}}{(1/4\pi) b_u \alpha_{ul} E_{ul} g N(\rm H_2)} \approx 4\times10^{-14}\ \rm s^{-1}$

answer_key.quantity: Gas density required for collisional suppression of higher-J H2 lines

evidence.loc: The case for a cosmic-ray contribution
evidence.quote: Both the illustrative CR redistribution calculation in Appendix 7 and the UV PDR models in Section 3.1 suggest that efficient collisional redistribution within the $v=1$ manifold becomes important at densities broadly of order $n_{\rm H}\sim10^{7}$–$10^{8},\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ in Oph 163131

score_reason: Archival ALMA products and public JWST/NIRSpec data are clearly identified, and the Meudon PDR code v7.0 and analytical rate equations are public/explicit, but exact spectral extraction aperture coordinates, integration windows, and full PDR input parameters are not specified.
rediscovery_reason: Main results are numeric H2 line surface brightnesses, line ratios (Table 1), and analytical/PDR model comparisons from public JWST (PID 5299) and ALMA archival data, though ALMA plays only a supporting morphological/context role.
